findings.body:
The comment (and the PR description) classify `codex` as a chat-completions leg that will apply complexity labels. In the runtime, `CodexProvider` subclasses `AgentRunnerProvider`, and `docs/PR_METADATA_CHECKS.md` marks complexity labeling as a no-op for all agent-runner providers (`cursor` / `claude-code` / `codex`). Only `provider: anthropic` will call `set_pr_complexity` and stamp `complexity:*`.

As written, maintainers will expect two legs to label and mis-debug a “missing” codex label. Fix the comment to match the matrix:

```suggestion
          # (anthropic) perform the assessment; agent-runner legs
          # (claude-code, cursor, codex) log a no-op warning by design.
```

This PR silently renames the dogfood gate from `ready` → `AIReview` (scope grep, `label-gate`, `empty_reason`, gate `if:`, and operator-facing messages). That is the bulk of the diff, but the PR title/body only describe enabling complexity labels, and the test plan still says “apply the `ready` label”.

Two concrete breakages follow:

1. **Doc cross-references now point at a section that does not exist.** Comments in this file cite `docs/TRIGGER_MODES.md § "Recipe: run once when labelled AIReview…"`, but that doc’s heading is still ``Recipe: run once when labelled `ready`…`` and still documents `ready` / `no-ready-label`.
2. **Contributor contract drift.** `AGENTS.md` still says self-review is “label-gated on `ready`”. After merge, agents and humans following AGENTS.md will apply the wrong label and never trigger dogfood.

Either split the rename into its own PR with AGENTS.md + `docs/TRIGGER_MODES.md` (+ any maintainer runbook) updated in lockstep, or restore `ready` here if the only intended change was complexity dogfooding.

summary:
## Verdict

Useful dogfood of `complexity-labels-enabled`, but the PR also renames the self-review gate label and mis-documents which providers actually apply complexity labels — both should be fixed before merge.

## Narrative

**What looks good.** Turning on complexity labeling in `self-review.yml` is the right dogfood surface for `docs/PR_METADATA_CHECKS.md`. Inputs match the public contract (`complexity-labels-enabled` + default `complexity-label-prefix: 'complexity:'`), permissions already include `pull-requests: write`, and the feature is best-effort / non-blocking on the runtime path. No new secrets, no shell interpolation of PR content, no third-party action pins.

**Findings.**

1. **Codex ≠ chat-completions for complexity labels** (`.github/workflows/self-review.yml` comment + PR body). Runtime `CodexProvider` is an `AgentRunnerProvider`; only `anthropic` will stamp `complexity:*`. Expect one label writer, not two — otherwise the test plan’s “confirm the anthropic leg” is fine, but any “codex should label too” expectation is wrong.

2. **Undocumented `ready` → `AIReview` rename.** Most of the diff is the gate rename (`label-gate`, scope grep, `empty_reason=no-gate-label`, gate `if:`, operator messages). That is a maintainer-facing contract change, not mentioned in the PR title/summary, and left `AGENTS.md` (“label-gated on `ready`”) and `docs/TRIGGER_MODES.md` (recipe still `ready` / `no-ready-label`) stale. Workflow comments even cite a TRIGGER_MODES section title that does not exist yet. After merge, following AGENTS.md applies the wrong label and dogfood never runs.

**Not raised as blockers.** Multi-leg races on the shared `complexity:*` label are inherent to the feature when several chat-completions legs run; with only anthropic applying labels today this is moot. `concurrency: cancel-in-progress` on the PR number is pre-existing and fine for label-toggle re-runs.

**PR hygiene.** Title says complexity-only; body test plan still says apply `ready`. Al
